text:
Maya Chen: quick thread — attached two comps: a mini welcome takeover (center, modal) and a compact shelf (bottom-left). which feels least disruptive for first-run? screenshots: https://img.redwood/test/onboard1.png and https://img.redwood/test/onboard2.png
Aisha (Design): i lean shelf — less interruption when folks are poking around. modal feels heavy for small quickstarts.
Devon Patel: shelf also cheaper on engineering side (no focus-trap shims). modal would need keyboard/focus polishing.
Maya Chen: fair — my main concern with shelf is discoverability for sample projects. CTA copy might need to be stronger.
Samir Iqbal: from experiments last quarter: persistent rail/shelf had ~12% higher CTA click than toast/modal, but modal had higher immediate engagement for the first 10s. tradeoffs: disruption vs conversion speed.
Oliver (a11y): both ok but key nits: modal must trap focus and restore focus on close; shelf needs visible keyboard focus states and ARIA live region if it appears. also CTA contrast on comp B is borderline (#5a8 -> needs AA).
Aisha (Design): thanks oliver — i'll raise contrast and add focus outline. copy options below — thoughts?
```
Copy A headline: "Try a sample project — get results in seconds"
CTA A: "Start sample"

Copy B headline: "Create your first project"
CTA B: "Create project"

Copy C headline: "Explore sample apps built on Redwood"
CTA C: "Browse samples"
```
Devon Patel: my vote is CTA A for shelf (short, verb-focused). for modal i'd use "Browse samples" since people are in a discovery mindset.
Samir Iqbal: metric callout — CTA phrasing matters: verbs + promise beat generic nouns by ~1.5x in our funnels. A/B test A vs C.
Maya Chen: ok action plan: 1) Aisha iterate shelf with CTA A + higher contrast 2) Devon add exp flag for shelf vs modal (10% each) 3) Oliver run quick a11y checklist on both comps 4) Samir to track funnel events (impression, click, project create).
Aisha (Design): putting new comps in Figma and will tag everyone by EOD :thumbsup:
Devon Patel: will stub feature flag: exp.onboard.takeover_vs_shelf.v1 -> rollout 10%. tagging for follow-up.
ConsoleBot: Experiment flag exp.onboard.takeover_vs_shelf.v1 created and enabled for 10% of new users.
Oliver (a11y): will run quick keyboard nav test once Aisha uploads updated frames. i'll post checklist results here. :eyes:
Maya Chen: great — thanks all. looping back after first week of data.
Devon Patel: FYI implementation note — shelf needs persist setting per-user ("don't show again") and an accessible dismiss touch target. i'll include that in the ticket.
Samir Iqbal: putting KPI deck on the shared board -> /drive/onboard-metrics. will share expected sample size for 10% rollouts.
Aisha (Design): assigned to @Aisha, @Devon, @Oliver. will ping when comps ready.
Maya Chen: cool, closing the loop here. :party_parrot:
